There are lots of things that can cause back pain and there are many possible "solutions".

Advising people to simply "squat" or to "strengthen the glutes" is not going to be the answer in all cases. If one has a dysfunctional SI joint, it can be dysfunctional in lots of ways that don't won't be resolved simply by simply increasing glute strength. For example, there may be an issue with proprioception (coordinated use of the joint).

Having said that, if one does have SI joint problems - a leading cause of back pain - squatting exercises can resolve the problem as long as one gives a lot of attention to "good" form relative to the problem.

  1. Squat with bodyweight to begin. Don't add weight until you have good control of the joint.
  2. Concentrate on controlling the SI joint as you squat
  3. Don't squat ass-to-grass until you have regained control of the joint.
  4. Try to stay very upright as you squat and don't allow any "but wink" to occur. The goal is to get proprioceptive control of the joint. If you sit all day in your job, maybe you have little control of the joint.
  5. Add weights (eg, hold weight plates)
  6. Once you are strong and have some control, maybe try to go to using a trap bar, but adjust it so you don't squat right down. Control that joint!

For overall spinal health, another good exercise is to learn to do calisthenic "bridges", where you hold your weight on your feet and hands and push the hips up to form a bridge as seen in "Convict Conditioning". This is a great spinal exercise as the spine is not well served with blood and this exercises not only strengthens and increases range of movement but it flushes out toxins and brings nutrients to the spine.
